finalText:
By default, React re-renders every child whenever the parent re-renders, no matter if the props changed. "Same props" doesn't skip a re-render on its own.

To skip it, you need two things together:

1. Wrap the child in `React.memo`.
2. Make sure the props are actually the same *by reference* — not just "look the same".

That second part trips people up most. If you pass an inline function or object, like `onClick={() => doThing()}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}`, React builds a brand new one every render. It looks identical, but it's a new object each time, so `memo` sees it as changed.

Fix: wrap the child in `memo`, and keep any function or object props stable with `useCallback` or `useMemo` in the parent.
